title.en: Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains (Master Wuyong Scroll)

museum_text.zh: 黃公望（西元一二六九－一三五四年），富陽人。字子久，號一峰，又號大癡道人，晚號井西道人。山水以董源為宗，為元四大家之冠。 此卷為僧無用所作，於至正七年（一三四七）起草，其年正八十歲。得暇即畫數筆，其中因曾外出旅行，至至正十年（一三五０），尚未完成。本卷筆端變化鼓舞，聖而神矣。
museum_text.en: The Yuan dynasty was a time when Taoism flourished and gave shelter to many scholars. Huang Kung-wang, having spent time in prison and with his hopes of an official career dashed, became a Taoist of the Full Truth Sect. He taught the Tao in the south-central Kiangnan region and became friends with such scholar-artists as Ts'ao Chih-po and Ni Tsan. He also taught painting, and "Secrets of Landscape Painting" may reflect his teachings. His landscape painting was influenced by Chao Meng-fu and his own enlightenment of the land. This scroll's depiction of fishermen as seen in his travels represents the culmination of his artistic career. Taking 4 years and finished in 1350, traces of his retouching are still seen, adding a dimension of time and thought. Done for Cheng Wu-yung, also a Taoist, it serves as a medium between the two.

intro.zh: 黄公望被馆方称为元四大家之首；1347年，八十岁的他开始为无用师画这卷画。
intro.en: Huang Gongwang, whom the museum ranks first among the Four Great Masters of the Yuan, began this scroll in 1347, at the age of eighty, for his friend Wuyong.

intro.zh: 他有空就画几笔；馆方的中文说明说到1350年仍未完成，英文说明则说历时四年、于1350年完成。
intro.en: He added a few strokes whenever he had time. The museum's Chinese text says it was still unfinished in 1350; its English text says it took four years and was finished that year.

intro.zh: 画的是富阳一带的富春山水，黄公望本人就是富阳人。
intro.en: It shows the scenery of the Fuchun Mountains at Fuyang, Huang's home district.

intro.zh: 1650年，收藏者吴洪裕临终前命人焚烧此画，想把它带到另一个世界；侄子吴静安把它救出，但画已烧成两段。
intro.en: In 1650 its owner, Wu Hongyu, had it burnt shortly before he died, so that he could take it to the afterlife; his nephew Wu Jing'an pulled it out, but it was already in two pieces.

intro.zh: 较短的前段《剩山图》在杭州的浙江省博物馆，较长的这一段在台北。
intro.en: The short opening piece, The Remaining Mountain, is in the Zhejiang Provincial Museum in Hangzhou; this long main section is in Taipei.

look_for.zh: 江上的渔人：馆方说画中的渔人来自他的游历见闻。
look_for.en: The fishermen on the river: the museum says they come from what he saw on his travels.

look_for.zh: 一层层的湿墨渲染和笔触。
look_for.en: Layer upon layer of wet ink washes and brushstrokes.

look_for.zh: 仍可看出他反复修改的痕迹，为画面添上了时间的维度。
look_for.en: Traces of his retouching, still visible, which add a dimension of time.

look_for.zh: 大片的空白，读作江水和雾气。
look_for.en: Long stretches of empty paper that read as water and mist.

alt.zh: 一幅极长而窄的淡墨手卷：起伏的山丘，岸边有树和小屋，中间是开阔的江面。
alt.en: A very long, narrow handscroll in pale ink: rolling hills, river banks with trees and small houses, and open water.

image_choice.note: The painting only; the museum image is the whole scroll, with later inscriptions.

who.zh: 李雪曼（Sherman E. Lee）与何惠鉴（Wai-kam Ho）
who.en: Sherman E. Lee and Wai-kam Ho

views.zh: 据维基百科对他们研究的转述，这卷画用一层层湿墨和笔触精心经营，看似随意，实则布局巧妙。
views.en: As Wikipedia summarises their study, the scroll was carefully built up in layers of wet washes and brushwork, so that it looks offhand while being inspired in its organisation.

views.zh: 真迹进入宫中时，他判定它是假的，坚持自己先得到的仿本才是真迹；这个错误直到1816年才被纠正。
views.en: When the genuine scroll reached his collection he judged it a fake, insisting that an imitation he already owned was the real one; the mistake was corrected only in 1816.

note.zh: 每一句都对照所注出处核对过；找不到可靠出处的说法已删去或改写。
note.en: Every sentence was checked against the sources it cites; claims without a reliable source were cut or rewritten.
